title: Six-class secp256k1 rho at 125.862153: pass 2's products by R on shared rows, R = 2^25, compares every 128th round

claims.statement: For a uniform full-production secp256k1 input Q=[x]P, the classical cold six-class negation-plus-GLV parallel Pollard-rho attack of proof.md and upstream-proof.md halts on every run with total work at most 2^125.862153 target-group-operation equivalents under classical-group-work-v2 (C=1000). It builds on bradcush's c06f6691 (125.8928: kaankolcu's 4ac17b66 with R = 2^25, the checkpoint compared every 128th round, h = 0.000065 and the round's reserve in its own word), whose walk, census, kappa, rows and fused pass 1 it keeps, with one kernel change: pass 2 forms R's rows B_i = R*2^(64i) mod p (i = 1..3, 4 instructions each) once per walk and computes both inv = R*acc and R' = R*dx on them (72 instructions each instead of 84), so pass 2 is 432.515625 instructions per walk and the ordinary step 127.03125 + 432.515625 + 25616/2^20 = 559.5713. The new row and fold exits return exact results (no new failure row); a walk takes at most 12 exits, so the round reserve is 320 milli-units per walk. The declared run executes pass 2 at that count against affine secp256k1, enters all 1,554 exit stubs (0 mismatches) and checks a limb port of the row product on every path. kappa = 1.0001 follows from the shipped hazard census as in c06f6691. Declared dependencies (proof.md section 6): c06f6691, 4ac17b66, 445f9a1c, cbea87bf, 4c8222cc, 673640ef, 0a1c5772, 610c8e49, 6a6cb91c, 5f1ae3ce, 4595bad7, 01488655, 2bd168b5, daf2c741, 4b4defe7, b78fb4f6, a9297fb0, 807e4bf5, b5de673a, 02feb284. Recovery probability is greater than 0.39000019 and therefore at least 0.39 (failure rows 1.0103e-7 < 1.1e-7). Peak memory is below 2^72 bytes; preprocessing is capped at 2^59 units, charged and included; nonuniform advice is zero. Exact ledger: S_ops = 1.0001*S0 = 2^126.6995433, phase 1 = 2^125.861937, hard extras = 2^111.149216, random extras = 2^98.8271, allowance = 2^112.7362, W_ledger = 2^125.8621523 <= 1000*2^125.862153 milli-units; Markov ratio 0.0000647188 < 0.000065; certificate.py checks the claim and that 125.862152 fails, in exact arithmetic. No prior acceptance, review verdict or official score is a premise. This is an analytic heuristic bound, not a practical break.

experiments.purpose: Part A: production secp256k1 checks of the walk identities and the canonical-index rule; Part B: a scaled toy pipeline of the checkpoint-only walk (even-y key, per-trail phases, compares every 128th round) on subgroups of y^2=x^3+7 with node routing, a check that the old and the production compare rule reach the same endpoints, and a long-trail trap test; kernels: Python limb ports of the field kernels against big integers, and the shipped loops (with rare exits on constructed inputs entering every stub), both copies of the fused pass 1, emitter wrappers and arrival rows executed by an AArch64 interpreter (kernels/a64.py) against affine secp256k1, a bit-exact model and the exact canonical rule, with instruction counts and the ledger recomputed. The toy run does not meter production instructions or implement 2^20 concurrent walks.
